title: Korean Pork Dumplings
description: A traditional Korean dish featuring ground pork and fermented ingredients, these dumplings are dense and packed with flavor, perfect for a midnight craving. They can be made with plant-based friendly ingredients for a vegetarian option.
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine ground pork, kimchi, tofu, green onions, garlic, and ginger, and mix well until all ingredients are fully incorporated.
Add sesame oil and soy sauce to the mixture and stir until everything is well combined.
Lay a dumpling wrapper on a flat surface and place a tablespoon of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper.
Dip your finger in a small amount of water and run it along the edge of the wrapper to help it stick together when sealed.
Fold the wrapper into a triangle by bringing the two opposite corners together to form a point, and press the edges together to seal the dumpling.
Repeat the process with the remaining wrappers and filling.
To cook the dumplings, bring a large pot of water to a boil and gently add the dumplings to the pot, being careful not to overcrowd it.
Cook the dumplings for 10-12 minutes, or until they float to the surface.
Remove the dumplings from the water with a slotted spoon and serve hot with your favorite dipping sauce.
Cook pork to an internal temperature of 63°C / 145°F and let it rest for 3 minutes before serving.
